holidays.name: National Stuffed Mushroom Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate bite-sized mushroom caps packed with cheese, breadcrumbs, herbs, sausage, or whatever delicious filling you can cram inside. Perfect for party appetizers and for fungi fans everywhere.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it grew out of the food-observance calendar of the internet age and has no single known founder. Stuffed mushrooms became popular at mid-20th-century American cocktail parties.
holidays.funFact: Stuffed mushrooms became a cocktail party staple in the 1950s and 60s, when hosts loved appetizers that could be made ahead and eaten in one bite.

holidays.name: World Cancer Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day uniting people to raise awareness, improve education, and take action against cancer. Not a silly day, but a very important observance on the quirky February calendar.
holidays.origin: Established in 2000 at the World Summit Against Cancer for the New Millennium in Paris, and now led by the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC).
holidays.funFact: The Paris summit that created the day also produced the Charter of Paris, a document aimed at speeding up research and improving patient care worldwide.

holidays.name: Create a Vacuum Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the art of creating a vacuum. Some celebrate with science experiments, while others use it as an excuse to finally clean the house, so the day sucks in all kinds of fans.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, humorous observance with murky origins that is often listed among the quirky science-themed days. It is not tied to any single founder or organization.
holidays.funFact: The first powered vacuum cleaner was patented by Hubert Cecil Booth in 1901, and it was so large that it was pulled by horses and parked outside buildings, with hoses fed through the windows.

holidays.name: Thank a Mail Carrier Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the people who brave snow, rain, heat, and grumpy dogs to bring your packages and letters to your door. Cookies and kind notes in the mailbox are encouraged.
holidays.origin: Started as a grassroots appreciation day, often observed on or around February 4 to honor postal workers across the United States.
holidays.funFact: The famous unofficial postal motto about neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night is not the official motto of the US Postal Service. It is inscribed on New York City's James Farley Post Office building.

holidays.name: Rosa Parks Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the civil rights icon whose refusal to give up her bus seat helped spark the Montgomery Bus Boycott. It is observed on her birthday in some US states with events, education, and remembrance.
holidays.origin: Rosa Parks was born on February 4, 1913, in Tuskegee, Alabama. California and Missouri recognize the day on February 4, while Ohio and Oregon observe it on December 1.
holidays.funFact: Parks had been an NAACP activist for years before her 1955 arrest, and she was trained in nonviolent protest at the Highlander Folk School.
